title: Provenance for data/metadata/solar_cycle_reference.csv

source.table: Table of minima, maxima and cycle durations (13-month smoothed monthly mean sunspot number, Version 2.0)
source.source_url_basis: SILSO page that publishes this table. The exact URL/export used to create the local file was NOT recorded at download time.
source.native_source_file_modified_time: 2026-10-22 19:55 (from the uploaded archive; not necessarily the retrieval time)
source.retrieval_date_note: Unrecorded. Fill in the real download date; 2026-10-22 is only the file modification date seen in the archive.

field_classification.published_precision: month (year + month only; no day-level dates exist in the source)

derived_here.end_date: = minimum_date of the NEXT cycle (shared boundary month). Blank for Cycle 25 because Cycle 26's minimum has not been published.
derived_here.status: completed if end_date exists, otherwise ongoing

field_classification.dropped_from_standardized_csv: Sunspot-number values at minima/maxima exist only in the native source file (columns SN).

boundary_convention: SILSO's published cycle duration is minimum-to-minimum. The derived start/end convention reproduces SILSO's published duration (years + months) for all 24 completed cycles. Consecutive cycles share the boundary month; no day-level boundary is implied.
date_format: YYYY-MM (month precision). No day was added.
sentinel_values: The -1 sentinels exist only in the SILSO monthly CSV and NOAA observed JSON, never in the reference table. Originals are never edited; src/solarshield_loaders.py converts -1 to NaN in memory only, in explicitly listed columns.

what_was_checked: On 2026-10-23 all 25 rows of the native file (cycle, minimum year/month/SN, maximum year/month/SN) were compared with the text of https://sidc.be/SILSO/cyclesmm as returned by a web search: 0 mismatches. This is a comparison with a page snapshot, not a byte-level comparison with the originally downloaded file.
Derived minimum-to-minimum durations equal SILSO's published durations for all 24 completed cycles (0 mismatches).
check_data.py cross-checks months against the NOAA smoothed series, which is derived from the same SILSO data, so it only catches transcription errors.
verification.claim: Dates are SILSO-published values as present in the native source file. They are NOT claimed to be independently verified.

open_items.text: Cycle 25 maximum_date is blank because the native source file has none. A different SILSO page (https://www.sidc.be/SILSO/cyclesminmax), as returned by a web search on 2026-10-23, lists a Cycle 25 maximum of 2024-10 (SN 160.9), while the cyclesmm page snapshot lists none. The two could not be reconciled here; the value was NOT added. Re-download the native table from SILSO and re-run scripts/build_solar_cycle_reference.py if you want it. Consistent with that page, the local NOAA 13-month smoothed series (through 2026-03) has its Cycle 25 high at 2024-10 (160.9); this is an observation from same-lineage data, not a declared SILSO maximum.
Retrieval date of the native source file is unrecorded.
Exact download URL/export of the native source file is unrecorded.
